classification.difficultyReason: Read six supplied interval diagrams and translate endpoint inclusion and ray direction into the explicitly taught set-builder notation. Negative mixed-number boundaries add familiar interpretation and exact notation, with no modelling or proof choice.

content.prompt: Use set notation to describe each interval.

spec.description: Unit ticks from −3 to 2; open endpoint at −2 and a rightward ray above the axis. TikZ is required because the supplied template schema has no interval-ray field.
spec.mathematics: All real numbers strictly greater than −2.
spec.answerVisibility: The interval graph is a permanent given; set notation is withheld.

answer.worked:
The open endpoint excludes $-2$, and the ray extends right, so $x>-2$.

$\{x:x>-2\}$

spec.description: Unit ticks from 0 to 5; closed endpoint at 4 and a leftward ray above the axis. TikZ preserves the interval ray, which is unsupported by the supplied template fields.
spec.mathematics: All real numbers less than or equal to 4.

answer.worked:
The filled endpoint includes $4$, and the ray extends left, so $x\le4$.

$\{x:x\le4\}$

spec.description: Unit ticks from −5 to 0; open endpoint at −2 and a leftward ray above the axis. The interval ray requires TikZ.
spec.mathematics: All real numbers strictly less than −2.

answer.worked:
The open endpoint excludes $-2$, and the ray extends left, so $x<-2$.

$\{x:x<-2\}$

spec.description: Unit ticks from 0 to 5; closed endpoint at 1 and a rightward ray above the axis. The interval ray requires TikZ.
spec.mathematics: All real numbers greater than or equal to 1.

answer.worked:
The filled endpoint includes $1$, and the ray extends right, so $x\ge1$.

$\{x:x\ge1\}$

spec.description: Integer ticks from −5 to 0 plus a labelled midpoint tick at −2½; closed endpoint there and a leftward ray. TikZ preserves the interval ray and additional isolated tick.
spec.mathematics: Endpoint −5/2 is included; the interval extends indefinitely left.

answer.worked:
The filled endpoint includes $-2\frac12$, and the ray extends left, so $x\le-2\frac12$.

$\{x:x\le-2\frac12\}$

spec.description: Integer ticks from −3 to 2 plus a labelled tick at −1⅔, one third of the way from −2 to −1; open endpoint there and a rightward ray. TikZ preserves the interval ray and additional isolated tick.
spec.mathematics: Endpoint −5/3 is excluded; the interval extends indefinitely right.

answer.worked:
The open endpoint excludes $-1\frac23$, and the ray extends right, so $x>-1\frac23$.

$\{x:x>-1\frac23\}$
